prompt: What does the lesson say the programs of the earlier lessons already are, because each exits with a status?

choices.text: Monitoring rules
choices.why: Those are lesson 22's, and they read counts.

choices.text: Tests
choices.why: Right: what they lacked was running on their own.

choices.text: Runbooks
choices.why: Runbooks are lesson 24's, and a person follows them.

choices.text: Approvals
choices.why: An approval is a name beside a version, not a program.

prompt: Why does the suite allow a failure to be KNOWN instead of leaving the check out until it is fixed?

choices.text: A suite that is red from day one teaches people to ignore red
choices.why: Right, and one that leaves the check out says nothing about it for ever.

choices.text: Known failures run faster than the others
choices.why: They run the same command.

choices.text: The keys of lesson 17 cannot be checked automatically
choices.why: keys.py checks them and exits 1.

choices.text: A known failure is fixed by the suite on its date
choices.why: The suite cannot fix anything; it reports.

prompt: Put the parts of a known failure in the order `suite.json` writes them.
items: the date it will be fixed by

prompt: How many checks were failing the build in the first run, before the approvals?
hint: The line above the exit status.

prompt: Why was the keys check OVERDUE rather than KNOWN?

choices.text: Its ticket had no reason written
choices.why: SEC-42 has a reason.

choices.text: Its fix was due on 5 October, before the run
choices.why: Right: past its date, a known failure fails like any other.

choices.text: keys.py exited with 2 instead of 1
choices.why: The verdict depends on the date, not on which non-zero status.

choices.text: Nobody approved the keys file
choices.why: Approvals are for the files under review, a different check.

prompt: The lesson's warning about exceptions: an exception with no ___ is a permanent hole.
hint: What does SEC-42 have that ran out?

prompt: Why does the candidate prompt wait in `data/candidates/` instead of `data/prompts/`?

choices.text: Candidates run at a higher temperature
choices.why: The temperature is a flag of rate.py.

choices.text: rate.py only reads that directory
choices.why: rate.py reads any file it is given.

choices.text: Lesson 18's budget does not cover new prompts
choices.why: Budgets are about spend, not review.

choices.text: Nothing goes into data/prompts/ unreviewed
choices.why: Right: every file there is under review.

prompt: In the single run at temperature 0, how many of the twelve tickets did the candidate fail?
hint: The second line of the block.

prompt: After one run each at temperature 0, two failures against three, what does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: The candidate is worse and should be refused
choices.why: That is the conclusion the intervals do not support.

choices.text: Nothing yet: one ticket is the whole difference
choices.why: Right: 5% to 45% against 9% to 53%.

choices.text: The current prompt should be rolled back
choices.why: Nothing showed it got worse.

choices.text: Temperature 0 makes the model deterministic, so it is proven
choices.why: One draw is one draw, deterministic or not.

prompt: Over 120 trials each, 24.2% against 31.7%, why is the gap still no proof?

choices.text: The intervals overlap; equal rates would give such a gap about one time in five
choices.why: Right: too often for the gap to prove anything.

choices.text: Wilson's interval only works above 1,000 trials
choices.why: It is built for small samples.

choices.text: The seeds were the same for both prompts
choices.why: Same seeds make the comparison fairer, not weaker.

choices.text: The rates were measured at temperature 0.8 instead of 0
choices.why: 0.8 is closer to production, which is the point.

prompt: Which advice does the lesson give for using a rate check, given what more trials cost? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Set a ceiling rather than compare two versions
choices.why: Yes: 120 trials can answer that.

choices.text: Grow the distinct cases before the runs
choices.why: Yes: twelve tickets re-asked are twelve situations.

choices.text: Keep the failures, not only the rate
choices.why: Yes: failures that move are a change to read.

choices.text: Re-run with new seeds until the result is stable
choices.why: Choosing among draws is the mistake the lesson names.

prompt: By how many times must the trials grow to halve the width of the interval?
Why did the candidate fail the build with an upper bound of 40.4%?
hint: The ceiling asks for something specific.

choices.text: Its measured rate, 31.7%, was over the ceiling
choices.why: 31.7% is under 40%; the upper bound is not.

choices.text: 120 trials could not show its rate is under 40%
choices.why: Right: a failure to show, not a finding that it is bad.

choices.text: The ceiling only accepts the current prompt
choices.why: The ceiling applies to any candidate.

choices.text: The overdue key stopped the rate check from running
choices.why: Both ran; the build has two reasons to be red.

prompt: Match each check to when the lesson runs it.
hint: One moment on the right belongs to no check.

pairs.right: when a file under review or a candidate changes

pairs.left: the rate of what is deployed

prompt: Why does the nightly run re-measure what is already deployed?

choices.text: Ollama clears its cache every night
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson depends on a cache.

choices.text: The suite cannot run during the day
choices.why: The suite runs in seconds at any time.

choices.text: Prices can change overnight and the ceiling follows them
choices.why: The ceiling is a failure rate, not a price.

choices.text: A hosted model can change with nothing in the repository changing
choices.why: Right: only a scheduled measurement notices.

prompt: Which job may hold the provider's key?

choices.text: Only jobs on code somebody with write access accepted
choices.why: Right: a fork's pull request could print it in its log.

choices.text: Every job, so the model check runs on every pull request
choices.why: That hands the key to anybody who opens a pull request.

choices.text: The suite, since it runs first
choices.why: The suite needs no key at all.

choices.text: None; the key goes in the repository beside ci.sh
choices.why: That is the leak lesson 17 found.

prompt: The build is red because a candidate's upper bound is just over the ceiling. Which response does the lesson rule out?

choices.text: Run more trials and see whether the interval comes down
choices.why: That is one of the honest choices.

choices.text: Drop the sentence the classifier never needed
choices.why: That is the other.

choices.text: Re-run with new seeds until one run passes
choices.why: Right: that is choosing the draw you liked.

choices.text: Read the failures to see which tickets moved
choices.why: Reading the failures is what the lesson asks for.

prompt: For the deterministic checks of the suite, a re-run gives the ___ answer.
